name: Chlorella extract

card.summary: Chlorella extract, from a green microalga, is used in skincare and supplements for its antioxidant and nucleotide-rich fractions that are proposed to support skin quality.
card.note: Intact cells are poorly digestible; supplement health claims have drawn FDA warning letters.

quick.overview:
Chlorella is a genus of single-celled green algae sold as a supplement and used in cosmetics. Extracts, including the nucleotide-rich "Chlorella Growth Factor" fraction, are discussed for skin quality and ageing.

The appearance chain is antioxidant and anti-glycation activity, then less skin damage, then a clearer, more youthful complexion. Research so far is laboratory-based.
quick.how: Chlorella appears in greens powders, tablets and topical products. T Nation users discuss it in greens-powder threads as part of a daily nutrition routine [1]. Cell walls must be broken for nutrients to be available [2].
quick.risks: Chlorella cell walls contain lipopolysaccharides that may affect the immune system [2]. The American Cancer Society states studies do not support claims of effectiveness against disease, and the FDA has sent warning letters over such claims [2].

lead: Chlorella is a genus of about 13 species of single-celled green algae, sold as a dietary supplement and used in cosmetics, health food and animal feed [2]. Chlorella extract usually refers to disrupted-cell fractions such as Chlorella Growth Factor (CGF), described as a nucleotide-rich, water-soluble intracellular fraction [3].

A 2026 review describes CGF as a heterogeneous metabolic fraction that may influence redox-sensitive pathways, extracellular matrix regulation and immune responses, while noting that most mechanistic evidence is indirect [3]. For appearance, a 2022 laboratory study found that Parachlorella beijerinckii extracts inhibited advanced glycation end products and glycative stress-induced inflammation in an in-vitro skin dermis-like model [4].
AGEs build up with age and are linked to wrinkles and loss of elasticity, which is why inhibiting them is of interest [4]. No human skin trial of chlorella extract was found.

chain: Chlorella extract supplies antioxidants and nucleotides
Reduced glycation and oxidative stress in lab models
angle.text: People take or apply chlorella extract hoping for better skin. The proposed route comes from laboratory work on glycation and redox pathways.

infobox: FDA warning letters over disease claims

paras: Chlorella is sold as a supplement and in cosmetics [2]. Greens powders that include it are discussed on T Nation [1].
CGF is described as a nucleotide-dominant fraction, not a classical receptor-binding growth factor [3]. Humans cannot digest intact chlorella cells, so cell walls must be broken [2].
A 2002 study found lipopolysaccharides in chlorella cell walls that can affect immunity; later work suggests they differ from those of Gram-negative bacteria [2].

Chlorella was used by Warburg and by Calvin in photosynthesis research, and mid-century hopes of mass-food use fell short because of cost [2]. Extracts have also been studied as a serum replacement in cell culture [5].
Related laboratory work includes the in-vitro skin dermis study of Parachlorella extracts [4] and a review of CGF mechanisms [3].

timeline.event: BIOS-3 experiment uses chlorella to balance CO2 and oxygen for one person [2].
